basis: All active titles were screened with their category; ambiguous targets were read using saved formulations, source excerpts, working summaries and source metadata. This is a topical review, not a new open-status verification.

decisions.title: The 1/3–2/3 conjecture
decisions.reason: An extremal balance statement about all finite partial orders. Its sorting application motivates retention, but the target is a combinatorial existence theorem rather than a data structure or running-time bound.

decisions.title: The gold partition conjecture
decisions.reason: An extremal guarantee on two successive partitions of the linear extensions of a partial order. Keep this beside the 1/3–2/3 question as a computationally motivated combinatorial boundary case.

decisions.title: Determine the pancake numbers
decisions.reason: The requested output is the exact extremal prefix-reversal distance over all permutations, rather than an efficient sorting implementation. It spans permutation combinatorics and restricted operations without requiring an algorithmic target.

decisions.title: Can execution bounded CRNs compute semilinear functions and predicates within polylogarithmic time?
decisions.reason: Execution-bounded chemical reaction networks use stochastic molecular timing and require all reaction sequences to cease. This unconventional computing model crosses complexity, distributed protocols and chemistry without a dedicated specialist category.

previous_override.reason: The question determines time complexity of computation in execution-bounded chemical reaction networks.

decisions.title: Does every class C with unbounded grid-width contain arbitrarily large connected monotone grid subclasses?
decisions.reason: The target is a structural containment theorem for permutation classes of unbounded grid-width. Its pattern-matching application does not make it a string algorithm, and its grid parameter is not an ordinary graph-width question.

decisions.title: Is graph isomorphism solvable in polynomial time?
decisions.reason: Classical polynomial-time graph-isomorphism testing has a clear home in the newly expanded static graph-algorithm category, alongside graph canonization.

decisions.title: For example, here is an open question that we have not addressed: for (say) the game Hex, does there necessarily exist a polynomial-size circuit that […]
decisions.reason: The Hex question asks for polynomial-size strategy circuits, so circuit complexity directly defines the target despite the game application.

decisions.title: What are the tradeoffs, if any, between the number of gates and the number of ancilla bits?
decisions.reason: The target is a gate-count versus workspace tradeoff for reversible Boolean circuits, directly within computational complexity.

decisions.title: The Classification of Reversible Bit Operations — Explicit open question on PDF page 2
decisions.reason: The saved question concerns quantum gate sets and intermediate quantum complexity classes, despite the classical-sounding paper title.

decisions.title: The Diameter of Caterpillar Associahedra — Explicit open question on PDF page 3
decisions.reason: The saved source asks for optimal static search trees in polynomial time. The associahedron title does not replace this direct data-structure target.

decisions.title: What Can Oracles Teach Us About the Ultimate Fate of Life? — Explicit open question on PDF page 5
decisions.reason: The saved question is the complexity of the limit language of a cellular automaton; it has a defined automata-theoretic target.

decisions.title: The Hartmanis–Stearns conjecture
decisions.reason: A real-time multitape Turing-machine restriction is the defining hypothesis. Keep the digit-generation/transcendence question in computational complexity.

decisions.title: Construction of mu-Limit Sets of Two-dimensional Cellular Automata — Explicit open question on PDF page 1
decisions.reason: Characterizing limit sets of cellular automata is directly about a specified automaton model.

decisions.title: Probabilistic cellular automata, invariant measures, and perfect sampling — Explicit open question on PDF page 5
decisions.reason: The implication between invariant-measure uniqueness and convergence is posed specifically for deterministic cellular automata.

decisions.title: Counting Polyominoes
decisions.reason: The target is enumeration and asymptotic counting of finite polyominoes, which fits Counting and enumeration.

decisions.title: 3-decomposition Conjecture
decisions.reason: A simultaneous edge decomposition of cubic graphs is directly structural graph theory.

previous_focus.reason: The remaining polynomial-time gap after Babai’s quasipolynomial algorithm is a canonical symmetry-recognition problem and a natural miscellaneous benchmark.
